summary: Added dry_run case: renders 'Stage skipped' with WP ID and stage name, plus badge-dry-run badge.
Added dry_run_no_ledger case: renders 'No ledger' with detail text, plus badge-dry-run badge.
Added dry_run_complete case: renders 'Dry run complete' with reason text, plus badge-dry-run badge.
Updated runEventSeverity() to map dry_run_no_ledger → run-event--warning and dry_run_complete → run-event--success; dry_run falls through to run-event--info.
Added 6 new tests to run-log.test.ts: content rendering and severity for each of the 3 new action types. All 41 targeted tests pass.

comments.note: The three new dry_run cases each declare fresh var bindings (wpId, stg, detail, reason) without shadowing issues, since each is inside its own block scope. However, the pattern of re-declaring 'wpId' in multiple case blocks (also done in stage_start, stage_complete, stage_error) means using var here is safe currently but would silently break if the switch were ever de-blocked. A future pass converting all var to const/let in these handlers would eliminate the risk entirely.

summary: Reviewed dry-run event rendering in run-log.js. All three new action cases (dry_run, dry_run_no_ledger, dry_run_complete) are correctly implemented: each prepends the badge-dry-run span, applies escapeHtml() to all user-content fields, and handles absent fields safely with empty-string fallbacks. runEventSeverity() correctly routes dry_run_no_ledger to warning and dry_run_complete to success, with dry_run falling through to info. All 5 acceptance criteria are met; 6 tests provide complete coverage of content rendering and severity mapping for each action type. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: The three new dry-run event cases prepend the badge before the action heading ('Dry Run' + 'Stage skipped'), while the run_start badge from WP-003 appends after the heading ('Run started' + badge). Both conventions are internally consistent with their respective event types — category-leading for dry-run action events, supplementary for run lifecycle events — but worth noting for future event card authors.

dry_run case applies escapeHtml(String(entry.stage).replace(/_/g, ' ')): the order is stringify → underscore-replace → HTML-escape, which is correct. The same underscore replacement is applied in stage_start and stage_complete, so the convention is consistent.
